{{< pagebreak >}}

## Necromancy Chains

Necromancy is the magic of the threshold, the doorway between life and death, and what happens when you hold it open. It drains life. It raises corpses. It reminds the living that their time is borrowed. Necromancers are feared for good reason. The power they wield is not evil by nature, but it's damn easy to use it that way.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Vampiric Touch Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*Drain life. Feed on the living. Trade their vitality for yours.*

#### Vampiric Touch (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Touch
**Duration:** Instantaneous
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** Your hand becomes a conduit to the grave. Your touch drains warmth and vitality, not enough to kill, but enough to remind the target of their mortality. The stolen life energy knits your wounds closed.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 2 necrotic damage. You regain 1 HP. |
| Standard (9-14) | 4 necrotic damage. You regain HP equal to half the damage dealt (round up). |
| Strong (15-18+) | 6 necrotic damage. You regain HP equal to the damage dealt. Excess healing becomes temporary HP that lasts 1 minute. |

*Touch of the grave. Vampiric Touch is a necromancer's first taste of the transaction: their life for yours. It's a dangerous spell, you have to be close enough to touch. But when you're wounded and the enemy is in your face, swapping some of their vitality for yours feels less like dark magic and more like justice.*

#### Greater Vampiric Touch (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Touch
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** One creature per round

**Description:** Your hand drips with shadow. For the spell's duration, you can make a melee spell attack each round, your touch drains life in great, gasping quantities and feeds it directly into you. This isn't a one-time transaction. This is a feeding.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 6 necrotic damage per touch. Heal for half. Spell lasts 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | 9 necrotic damage per touch. Heal for half. You can make one touch attack each round for 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 12 necrotic damage per touch. Heal for half. Each successful touch also weakens the target, it has Bane on its next attack. You gain +1 Armor (stacks up to +3) as stolen vitality shields you. |

*The spell that makes you a monster, in the best possible way. Greater Vampiric Touch turns you into a melee threat that gets stronger as the fight goes on. Every round, you hurt them and heal yourself. The math of attrition bends in your favor. Your allies may look at you differently afterward. Let them. You're still standing.*

#### Finger of Death (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Water
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 60 feet
**Duration:** Instantaneous
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** You point, and death answers. Negative energy, the raw stuff of un-life, pours through your finger in a black ray. A creature killed by this spell doesn't just die. It rises, immediately, as a zombie under your control. Forever.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 9 necrotic damage. Target is sickened, Bane on attacks for 1 round. |
| Standard (9-14) | 15 necrotic damage. A humanoid killed by this damage rises at the start of your next turn as a zombie permanently under your control (max 1 zombie from this spell at a time). |
| Strong (15-18+) | 21 necrotic damage. A creature killed rises as a zombie. You may have up to 3 Finger of Death zombies at once. The zombie retains the base physical stats it had in life. |

*The signature spell of necromancy. Finger of Death doesn't just kill, it recruits. Every enemy you drop with this spell becomes another soldier in your growing army. The BBEG's most loyal lieutenant? Now she's your most loyal lieutenant. She's not happy about it. She doesn't get a vote.*

### Animate Dead Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*Raise the fallen. Build your army from the enemy's casualties.*

#### Raise Skeleton (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 minute
**Range:** Touch
**Duration:** 1 hour
**Target:** One corpse or pile of bones

**Description:** You infuse a dead body with a spark of animating energy. The skeleton pulls itself free of the rotting flesh, or assembles itself from scattered bones, and stands awaiting your command. It's mindless, obedient, and completely disposable.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The skeleton is fragile, 5 HP, attacks at -2. Duration 10 minutes. |
| Standard (9-14) | Skeleton has 10 HP. Uses your skill ranks for attacks. Simple commands only, guard, attack, carry. Duration 1 hour. |
| Strong (15-18+) | As Standard, but the skeleton has 15 HP and can follow moderately complex commands, "guard this door and attack anyone who isn't wearing a blue cloak." Duration 2 hours. |

*Your first soldier. Raise Skeleton gives you an extra pair of bony hands, a flanking partner, a trap-tester, a silent sentry who doesn't need to sleep. It won't win fights on its own, but it'll take hits meant for you. And there's something to be said for sending a skeleton through every doorway first.*

#### Animate Dead (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 minute
**Range:** Touch
**Duration:** 24 hours
**Target:** Up to 3 corpses

**Description:** You reach into the space between life and death and pull. Multiple corpses stir. Flesh knits with shadow. Eyes that saw nothing now see only your will. You raise up to three skeletons or zombies, or reassert control over undead you've already created.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 1 skeleton or zombie. 10 HP. Simple commands. Duration 1 hour. |
| Standard (9-14) | Up to 3 skeletons/zombies. Each has 15 HP. They act on your initiative as a group. You can give them a standing order they'll follow until completed. Duration 24 hours. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Up to 5 undead. 20 HP each. They can follow moderately complex orders. One of them may be a zombie that retains fragments of its living skills, it can use one weapon proficiency or skill it had in life. |

*Now you have a squad. Animate Dead turns a fresh battlefield into a recruitment drive. Three bodies become three soldiers. They don't complain. They don't need pay. They don't question orders. The living have limits. The dead have your permission.*

#### Create Undead (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Earth
**Casting Time:** 1 hour
**Duration:** Permanent until destroyed
**Target:** Up to 3 corpses

**Description:** This is not animation, it's creation. You forge undead with purpose and power. Ghouls with paralytic claws. Wights that drain life with every strike. These are not mindless servants, they're weapons with instincts, loyal only to you, existing only to fulfill your commands.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 2 ghouls. 25 HP each. Claw attack (9 slashing + paralysis on Strong). Simple commands. Permanent. |
| Standard (9-14) | 3 ghouls or 1 wight. Ghouls as above. Wight: 40 HP, longsword (15 slashing), life drain touch (15 necrotic, heals wight). Intelligent enough for tactical commands. Permanent. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 3 wights or 1 wraith. Wights as above. Wraith: 50 HP, incorporeal, touch deals 21 necrotic. Can phase through walls. Intelligent and malevolent. Permanent. |

*This is the spell that makes kingdoms nervous. Create Undead gives you permanent, intelligent, self-directed minions. They don't expire at dawn. They don't forget their orders. They wait in the dark, forever, for your command. Use this spell carefully. The dead remember who made them, and they're patient.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

## Transmutation Chains

Transmutation is the magic of becoming. It reshapes flesh, bone, and steel. It speeds the body beyond natural limits. It turns skin to stone and stone to diamond. Transmuters are engineers of the physical form. They don't destroy, they transform. What emerges from their magic is stronger, faster, and harder than what went in.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Haste Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*Speed beyond nature. Move faster, hit harder, do more.*

#### Enhance (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Touch
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** You infuse the target with magical vigor. Muscles twitch with energy. Reflexes sharpen. For the next minute, they're just a little bit better at everything physical, not superhuman, but the best version of themselves.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | +1 to one physical attribute (Brawn, Fortitude, or Agility) for 1 minute. |
| Standard (9-14) | +1 to two physical attributes for 1 minute. Target's speed increases by 5 feet. |
| Strong (15-18+) | +1 to all three physical attributes for 1 minute. Speed +10 feet. Target gains one additional reaction during the duration. |

*The first transmutation most mages learn. Enhance doesn't transform, it optimizes. Your Blade hits a little harder. Your Protector holds the line a little longer. Your own legs carry you a little faster when it's time to not be where the dragon is breathing.*

#### Haste (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** Time bends around the target. They move in a blur, striking twice where they'd strike once, crossing the battlefield between heartbeats, catching arrows out of the air. When the spell ends, the target crashes hard. Haste is a loan, and the body always pays it back with interest.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Target gains +1 action per round (attack or move only). Speed +10. Duration 3 rounds. No crash. |
| Standard (9-14) | Speed doubled. +2 Armor (time to dodge). One additional action per round, attack, move, or use an object. Duration 1 minute. When the spell ends, the target loses its next action (crash). |
| Strong (15-18+) | As Standard, but speed tripled. The additional action can be anything except casting a spell of Adept tier or higher. The target's attacks have Boon against creatures that haven't acted yet this round. Crash is only a lost reaction. |

*The best buff in the game, bar none. Haste turns your Blade into a food processor. Your Protector into a wall that's everywhere at once. Yourself into a problem that's already solved by the time the enemy realizes there's a problem. The crash at the end is real, but if the fight's not over by then, you used Haste wrong.*

#### Time Stop (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Wind
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** 2-5 rounds of apparent time
**Target:** Self

**Description:** You step between the ticks of the clock. Time stops for everyone but you. The world freezes, arrows hang in the air, spells pause mid-detonation, enemies are statues. You have a handful of subjective rounds to act before reality catches up and remembers it was supposed to be moving.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Time stops for 1d2 rounds. You cannot directly harm creatures during the stop, offensive spells and attacks break the effect. You can move, manipulate objects, and cast non-offensive spells. |
| Standard (9-14) | Time stops for 1d4+1 rounds. You can act freely, attack, cast, move, use items. Damage is applied simultaneously when time resumes. You cannot affect creatures outside a 30-foot radius of your starting position. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Time stops for 1d4+2 rounds. No range limit on your actions. You may cast one Master-tier spell during the stop without expending its per-session use, the time magic pays the cost. When time resumes, all your actions resolve in the order you performed them. |

*This is why transmuters are terrifying. Time Stop gives you 12 to 30 seconds of subjective time in a frozen world. Walk through the enemy formation. Place a Fireball at every exit. Read the villain's diary over their shoulder. Empty their component pouch. Then resume time and watch everything happen at once. The ultimate transmutation isn't changing matter, it's changing the rules of cause and effect.*

### Stone Skin Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*Transform your body. Become harder. Become untouchable.*

#### Stone Skin (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 10 minutes
**Target:** Self

**Description:** Your skin hardens and grays, taking on the texture and resilience of granite. You move a little slower, but blades that would have cut deep now chip and skitter across your surface.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | +1 Armor. Speed reduced by 5 feet. Duration 1 minute. |
| Standard (9-14) | +2 Armor. Resistance to non-magical slashing and piercing damage. Speed reduced by 5 feet. Duration 10 minutes. |
| Strong (15-18+) | +3 Armor. Resistance to all non-magical physical damage. No speed reduction, the stone moves with you. |

*Armor for the naked mage. Stone Skin is the spell you cast before the fight starts, when you know you're walking into a storm of steel. You're harder to hurt, harder to move, harder to kill. The enemy will break their weapons on you, and you'll still be standing when they run out of sharp things.*

#### Iron Body (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** Self

**Description:** Your flesh transmutes to living iron. You're heavier, denser, and almost impossible to damage with conventional weapons. Your fists hit like warhammers. Fire, ice, and lightning wash over you with diminished effect. You are, for one minute, a walking siege engine.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | +3 Armor. Unarmed strikes deal 2 bludgeoning. Speed halved. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | +4 Armor. Unarmed strikes deal 4 bludgeoning. Resistance to fire, ice, and lightning. Immune to poison and disease. Speed halved. You weigh 500 pounds, wooden floors may not support you. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | +5 Armor. Unarmed strikes deal 6. Resistance to all elemental damage. Immune to poison, disease, and critical hits. Speed is normal, the iron is somehow weightless to you. You can punch through stone walls. |

*You are now the party's Protector, regardless of what your character sheet says. Iron Body doesn't make you harder to hurt. It makes hurting you a bad idea. Walk into melee. Let them swing. When their blades shatter and their spells fizzle, smile with your iron teeth and remind them why transmuters don't need bodyguards.*

#### Diamond Form (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Earth
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** Self

**Description:** Your body crystallizes into living diamond. Light refracts through you in prismatic bursts. You are nearly invulnerable, the hardest substance in existence, shaped like a person, moving with lethal purpose. Spells bounce off you. Weapons shatter on contact. You are the pinnacle of defensive transmutation, and for one minute, nothing in the world can break you.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | +4 Armor. Unarmed strikes deal 9. Resistance to all damage. Speed halved. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | +5 Armor. Unarmed strikes deal 15. Resistance to all damage. Immune to critical hits and precision damage. Spells of Adept tier or lower reflect off you, the caster takes the effect instead. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | +6 Armor. Unarmed strikes deal 21. Immunity to all damage except force. Spells of any tier that target only you are reflected. Your body emits bright light in a 30-foot radius, undead and fiends in the light take 4 radiant damage per round. You can walk through walls by crystallizing and recrystallizing on the other side. |

*This is what perfection looks like. Diamond Form is the ultimate defensive transmutation, your body becomes the hardest substance in creation, and magic itself bounces off your crystalline skin. For one minute, you're not a combatant. You're a force of nature. The enemy can't hurt you, can't spell you, can't stop you. When the diamond mage walks into the room, the room changes. Usually by evacuating.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

## Earth Chains

Earth magic is the magic of patience and inevitability. Stone doesn't burn. Stone doesn't bend. Stone waits, and then it falls, and everything in its path is reminded that the ground beneath their feet is not a floor, it's a weapon. Earth mages don't chase the enemy. They make the enemy come to them, then they bury them.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Stone Spikes Chain
**Disciplines:** Earth
*The fundamental earth chain. From jagged floor to shaking ground to splitting earth.*

#### Stone Spikes (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Earth
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 60 feet
**Duration:** 1 minute
**Target:** 10-foot radius

**Description:** The ground erupts in a field of razor-sharp stone spikes. Anything moving through the area gets torn up. Anything standing still when the spikes erupt gets a very pointed lesson in geology.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 2 earth damage to creatures in the area when cast. The spikes are sparse, creatures can navigate them with care. |
| Standard (9-14) | 4 earth damage to creatures in the area when cast. Spikes persist for 1 minute. Creatures entering or moving through the area take 2 earth damage per 5 feet moved. Area is difficult terrain. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 6 earth damage to creatures in the area when cast. Spikes persist for 1 minute. Any creature knocked prone in the area takes an additional 3 earth damage as the spikes find flesh. |

*Your first real earth spell. It doesn't chase. It doesn't seek. It waits. Drop it in a doorway. Drop it under the enemy formation. Let them bleed for every inch. Earth magic rewards positioning, and Stone Spikes rewards it with interest.*

#### Earthquake (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Earth
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 100 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** 30-foot radius

**Description:** The ground bucks and heaves like a wounded animal. Cracks split the earth. Structures groan and collapse. Anyone standing in the area is thrown off their feet, battered by debris, and reminded that the planet is not as solid as they've been led to believe.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 6 earth damage in a 20-foot radius. Creatures are knocked prone on a failed Agility check. Cracks appear but don't fully split. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | 9 earth damage per round in a 30-foot radius. Creatures must make an Agility check each round or be knocked prone. Structures take double damage. Fissures open in the ground, 10 feet deep. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 12 earth damage per round in a 40-foot radius. Creatures have Bane on Agility checks to stay standing. Fissures are 20 feet deep and creatures falling in take additional falling damage. Structures within the radius automatically collapse on a Strong result. |

*Earthquake is area denial on a geological scale. You drop it on the enemy fortification and watch the walls come down. You drop it on the charging cavalry and watch the horses panic and the riders tumble into cracks that weren't there a moment ago. When the ground is your weapon, there is no safe place to stand.*

#### Fissure (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Earth, 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 150 feet
**Duration:** Instantaneous (terrain permanent)
**Target:** A line 60 feet long, 10 feet wide

**Description:** You point at the ground and the world splits open. A chasm yawns where there was solid earth. Anything standing on the line falls. Anything on the edges scrambles. The crack doesn't close. The landscape is permanently altered. You've drawn a line on the map, and the map will never be the same.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 30-foot line, 10 feet wide, 20 feet deep. 9 earth damage to creatures falling in. The chasm is permanent. |
| Standard (9-14) | 60-foot line, 15 feet wide, 40 feet deep. 15 earth damage to creatures falling in. Creatures within 10 feet of the edge must make an Agility check or fall in. The fissure cuts through non-magical structures. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 80-foot line, 20 feet wide, 60 feet deep. 21 earth damage to creatures falling in. Creatures within 20 feet of the edge must make a Hard Agility check or fall in. The fissure cuts through magical structures of Adept tier or lower. Lava seeps from the bottom, dealing 5 fire damage per round to anyone inside. |

*The spell that splits battlefields. Fissure doesn't just damage, it divides. You draw a line between the enemy and their reinforcements. Between the villain and their escape route. Between your party and whatever's chasing them. The crack in the ground is permanent. The tactical implications are permanent. Earth magic's final answer to the question "how do I control the entire battlefield?"*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Wind Chains

Wind magic is the art of motion. It doesn't destroy, it *relocates.* It doesn't burn, it *blows out.* Wind mages control the space between things: the distance between an archer and their target, the footing of a charging knight, the trajectory of a falling ally. Fire mages burn the world. Wind mages move it around until it looks the way they want.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Gust Chain
**Disciplines:** Wind
*The fundamental wind chain. From a shove of air to a howling gale that reshapes the battlefield.*

#### Gust (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Wind
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** Instantaneous
**Target:** One creature or object up to 100 pounds

**Description:** A concentrated blast of wind slams into your target. It's not enough to kill. It's enough to move. And sometimes, moving is all you need.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Target is pushed 5 feet. Small unattended objects (papers, cloaks, torches) are scattered. |
| Standard (9-14) | Target is pushed 10 feet or knocked prone (your choice). Objects up to 100 pounds are blown 15 feet. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Target is pushed 20 feet and knocked prone. You may also extinguish all non-magical flames within 15 feet of the target or fan existing flames to double their radius for 1 round. |

*The first lesson of wind magic: you don't need to hurt something to beat it. Gravity does the hurting for you. Gust is a geometry spell. Ledges, pits, campfires, unstable bridges, the battlefield is full of weapons waiting for a nudge. Be the nudge.*

#### Wind Wall (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Wind
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 60 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** A wall up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, 5 feet thick

**Description:** A roaring curtain of wind springs into existence. Arrows curve around it. Gases and clouds dissipate on contact. Small creatures that try to pass through get flung backward like they've been swatted by an invisible giant. The wall howls. The wall *judges.*

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 15-foot wall, 10 feet high. Ranged attacks through the wall have Bane. Small flying creatures cannot pass. |
| Standard (9-14) | 30-foot wall. Ranged attacks through the wall automatically miss (non-magical ammunition). Creatures passing through take 6 bludgeoning damage and are pushed back 10 feet. Gas, fog, and smoke cannot cross. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 50-foot wall. As Standard, plus creatures attempting to pass through take 9 bludgeoning and are knocked prone on the far side. The wall can be shaped into a ring up to 15 feet in diameter. |

*The archer's nightmare. Wind Wall says "this direction is closed." Put it between your party and the enemy archers. Put it across a bridge. Put it in front of a charging formation and watch them stumble as their momentum meets a wall of angry air. Wind magic doesn't kill. It frustrates. And frustration wins fights.*

#### Whirlwind (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Wind, 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 100 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** 15-foot radius, 40 feet high

**Description:** A tornado touches down where you point. It's not the full fury of nature, but it's close enough. Creatures are sucked in, spun around, and flung out like dice from a cup. Debris becomes shrapnel. The battlefield becomes a blender.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 10-foot radius whirlwind. 9 bludgeoning damage per round to creatures inside. Creatures ending their turn inside are flung 15 feet in a random direction and knocked prone. |
| Standard (9-14) | 15-foot radius. 15 bludgeoning damage per round. Creatures must make a Brawn check to resist being pulled 10 feet toward the center each round. Creatures flung take an additional 5 damage if they strike a solid surface. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 20-foot radius. 21 bludgeoning damage per round. Brawn checks to resist the pull have Bane. The whirlwind picks up debris that deals 4 slashing damage to all creatures within 20 feet of its edge. You can move the whirlwind 20 feet per round as part of your action. |

*The wind mage's masterpiece. Whirlwind isn't just damage, it's chaos. Enemies are picked up, spun around, and deposited somewhere else with considerably less dignity and considerably more bruising. The formation collapses. The careful positioning unravels. And through it all, you stand at the center of the calm, directing the storm with a finger.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Fear Chains

Fear magic is the art of the flinch. It doesn't draw blood. It doesn't break bones. It breaks the thing behind the eyes, the part that says "I can win this." Fear mages don't fight the enemy. They make the enemy fight themselves, and the enemy always loses that fight.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Cause Fear Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*The fundamental fear chain. From a whisper of doubt to a scream that unravels armies.*

#### Cause Fear (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** You reach into the target's mind and find the thing they're most afraid of. Then you show it to them. It's not real. They know it's not real. Their body doesn't care. Their heart is already racing. Their hands are already shaking. They're already backing away.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The target is shaken, -1 on attacks for 1 round. |
| Standard (9-14) | The target is frightened. It has Bane on attacks and must use its move to retreat from you each round. It gets a Reason check each round to shake it off. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | The target is terrified. Bane on attacks and checks. It must flee from you by the fastest available means. If cornered, it cowers and cannot act. Reason checks to resist have Bane. |

*The first fear spell. It won't kill anyone. It'll just make them not want to be anywhere near you. Drop it on the enemy commander. Drop it on the charging ogre. Drop it on anyone whose confidence is their primary weapon. Fear doesn't need to hurt. It just needs to be believed.*

#### Fear (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self (30-foot cone)
**Duration:** Instantaneous (fear persists 1 minute)
**Target:** All creatures in a 30-foot cone

**Description:** You open your mouth and what comes out isn't a sound, it's pure terror given voice. Every creature in the cone experiences their worst fear simultaneously. Weapons drop. Bladders empty. Courage evaporates. The ones in the back are already running. The ones in the front wish they were.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Creatures in a 15-foot cone are shaken for 1 round. -1 on attacks and checks. |
| Standard (9-14) | Creatures in a 30-foot cone are frightened for 1 minute. Bane on attacks, must flee from you. They drop whatever they're holding. Reason check each round to recover. |
| Strong (15-18+) | As Standard, but creatures are terrified and have Bane on the Reason check to recover. Creatures that fail their first Reason check take 6 psychic damage as their own mind turns against them. |

*The spell that ends charges. Fear doesn't discriminate. The veteran knight and the fresh conscript both have something they're afraid of, and you just showed it to both of them at the same time. The cone isn't a weapon. It's a door, and behind the door is everything the enemy has ever had a nightmare about.*

#### Phantasmal Killer (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Wind
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 60 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** You don't just show them their fear. You give it teeth. You give it claws. You give it their mother's voice and their father's disappointed stare. The nightmare becomes flesh, visible only to the target, and it wants them dead. And because their mind believes it, their body believes it, and belief is fatal.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The target is frightened and takes 9 psychic damage. The killer form is indistinct, a shape in the corner of their eye. Reason check each round to disbelieve. |
| Standard (9-14) | The target is terrified and takes 15 psychic damage per round. The killer is vivid and relentless. The target attacks the phantasm (which cannot be harmed) unless it passes a Hard Reason check each round. Allies of the target cannot see the killer and cannot convince the target it isn't real. |
| Strong (15-18+) | As Standard, but psychic damage is 21 per round. The Reason check is Near-Impossible. The phantasm takes the form of the target's deepest, most specific fear, tailored by your knowledge of the target if you have any. If the target dies from this damage, their heart stops from pure terror, and their face freezes in an expression that will haunt whoever finds the body. |

*This is fear magic's final form. Not a trick, not a scare, an assassination performed by the target's own psyche. Phantasmal Killer is personal. It's intimate. It's cruel. You're not attacking their body. You're attacking the one thing they can't armor, can't dodge, and can't outrun: their own mind. When it's over, there's no wound to explain. Just a corpse with a face full of terror and a heart that forgot how to beat.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Arcane Ward Chains

Arcane wards are the shield before the sword. They don't hurt the enemy. They make hurting you a losing proposition. Ward mages are the quiet ones at the back of the party who everyone ignores until the dragon's breath washes over the group and everyone except the ward mage is on fire. Then they're the most popular person in the room.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Arcane Ward Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*Layered magical defense. From a personal bubble to a fortress of reflected magic.*

#### Arcane Ward (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Touch
**Duration:** 10 minutes
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** You weave a shimmering layer of protective magic around the target. It's invisible until struck, then it flares for an instant, absorbing the blow before fading. Think of it as armor made of math. It's not heavy. It's not restrictive. It's just there, and when something hits it, it's suddenly very busy being somewhere else.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The ward has 2 absorption. The next 2 points of damage the target takes are negated, then the ward fades. |
| Standard (9-14) | The ward has 4 absorption. Absorbs damage from any source. When it breaks, the excess damage carries over to the target. Duration 10 minutes or until depleted. |
| Strong (15-18+) | The ward has 6 absorption. As Standard, plus the first attack that breaks the ward causes a flash of light, the attacker has Bane on its next attack as it blinks away the glare. |

*Insurance. Pure, simple, magical insurance. You cast Arcane Ward on yourself before the dungeon. You cast it on the Protector before the boss fight. You cast it on the rogue before they try to disarm a trap they probably shouldn't be touching. It won't stop a determined enemy, but it'll buy you one more round. And one more round is all a good party needs.*

#### Spell Shield (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 reaction (when you or an ally within 30 feet is targeted by a spell)
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** Instantaneous
**Target:** One creature

**Description:** A lattice of counter-spell energy springs up between the target and an incoming spell. The hostile magic hits the lattice and shatters, its energy dispersed into harmless sparkles and the faint smell of ozone. You don't just block the spell. You unmake it.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The triggering spell's effect is reduced. Area spells shrink by half radius. Damage spells deal half damage. Debilitating effects grant the target Boon on any check to resist. |
| Standard (9-14) | The triggering spell is negated entirely if it's Adept tier or lower. Novice spells are reflected back at the caster. The shield leaves a residual glow, the target has +2 on checks against the next magical effect within 1 round. |
| Strong (15-18+) | The spell is negated regardless of tier (even Master). It is reflected back at the caster. The target gains +2 Armor against all magical damage for 1 round, and you regain one use of a Novice spell you have already used this encounter. The shield's feedback loop didn't just block, it harvested. |

*The reason ward mages are feared by other casters. Spell Shield is a reaction. You cast it when the Fireball is already in the air, when the Dominate is already reaching for your ally's mind. And then the Fireball isn't in the air anymore. And the Dominate is suddenly very interested in the caster who sent it. There's no better feeling in magic than watching an enemy caster's spell turn around and bite them.*

#### Spell Turning (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Protection
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** Self

**Description:** You surround yourself with a shimmering sphere of reflective magic. Spells that target you don't just fail. They bounce. They ricochet back at their caster with full force. For the duration, you are a mirror. The enemy's magic becomes your weapon, and every caster on the battlefield learns very quickly to point their spells somewhere else.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Spells of Novice tier or lower that target you are reflected back at the caster. 3 charges, then the sphere fades. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | Spells of Adept tier or lower are reflected. Area spells that include you in their radius are negated for you only. 5 charges. You may choose to let beneficial spells through without consuming a charge. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Spells of any tier are reflected. Area spells have their center point shifted to the caster's location instead of yours. Unlimited charges for the duration. When the spell ends, any remaining charges detonate in a harmless but spectacular light show, and every caster within 100 feet knows exactly what you just did. |

*This is the spell that makes enemy mages retire. Spell Turning doesn't just protect you, it punishes anyone who tries to magic you. The enemy Arcanist winds up their biggest spell and you just smile. They cast. The spell hits your sphere. The sphere considers the spell for a moment, finds it wanting, and sends it back with a note that says "try again." The look on their face when their own Disintegrate comes home is worth every discipline point you spent to get here.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Summoning Chains

Summoning is the magic of calling. You don't create. You don't transform. You reach across the boundaries between worlds, between planes, between the living and the not-living, and you pull something through. Summoners are never alone. They're never outnumbered. They're never out of options. They just need a minute, and something from somewhere else will arrive to solve the problem.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Summon Familiar Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*From a watchful spirit to an elemental ally to a bound planar entity.*

#### Summon Familiar (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 hour
**Range:** 10 feet
**Duration:** Permanent until dismissed or the familiar dies
**Target:** An unoccupied space within range

**Description:** You call a minor spirit and bind it into the form of a small animal, a cat, an owl, a raven, a spider, a snake. The familiar is intelligent, telepathically linked to you, and utterly loyal. It can't fight, not really, but it can watch, listen, and deliver touch spells from a safe distance while you stay very far away.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The familiar arrives but is skittish. It can relay simple impressions (danger, food, light, dark) telepathically within 30 feet. |
| Standard (9-14) | A loyal familiar of your chosen form. Telepathic link within 100 feet. You can see through its eyes and hear through its ears as an action. It can deliver touch-range spells you cast. It has 5 HP and uses your skill ranks for any checks it makes. |
| Strong (15-18+) | As Standard, but the familiar is particularly clever. It can speak one language you know. It can use the Help action to grant Boon to an ally within 5 feet. It can carry objects up to 5 pounds. Its bond to you is strong enough that if it dies, it can be resummoned after a long rest without expending resources. |

*Your first companion from beyond. The familiar won't win fights. It will, however, scout the next room, watch your back while you sleep, and deliver a Greater Vampiric Touch to an enemy while you're thirty feet away and pretending to be harmless. Treat it well. It's not a tool. It's a friend who happens to be made of spirit-stuff and moonlight.*

#### Conjure Elemental (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 minute
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 hour
**Target:** An unoccupied space within range

**Description:** You open a doorway to an elemental plane and call something through. Fire, earth, water, or air, you choose the element. What answers is a being of raw elemental fury, bound to your will for the duration. It's not friendly. It's not tame. It's a piece of a hurricane or a volcano given form, and it's very confused about why it's here. But it will fight for you, because the binding says so.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | A lesser elemental appears. 25 HP. Its attacks deal 6 damage of its element. It follows simple commands. If you lose concentration, it turns hostile instead of vanishing. Duration 10 minutes. |
| Standard (9-14) | A full elemental appears. 50 HP. Attacks deal 9 damage. It can follow tactical commands and act independently to fulfill your intent. If concentration breaks, it vanishes. Duration 1 hour. |
| Strong (15-18+) | A greater elemental. 75 HP. Attacks deal 12 damage of its element + a secondary effect (fire ignites, ice slows, lightning stuns, earth knocks prone). It fights with intelligence and can use one special ability of its element (a fire elemental's immolation aura, an air elemental's whirlwind). If concentration breaks, it vanishes rather than turning hostile. |

*Your first real army. An elemental isn't subtle. It's a walking natural disaster that happens to be on your side. Drop a fire elemental into the enemy camp. Send an earth elemental through the fortress wall. Put an air elemental between your party and the incoming arrows. The elemental doesn't care about tactics. It cares about the binding, and the binding says "do what the mage says."*

#### Planar Binding (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Earth
**Casting Time:** 1 hour
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** Permanent until broken
**Target:** One elemental, fey, fiend, or celestial

**Description:** You don't summon. You *bind.* You call a creature from another plane, something intelligent, something powerful, and you trap it in a circle of your will. It must serve. It can negotiate. It can bargain. It can plead. But at the end of the hour, it either agrees to your terms or it stays in that circle until the stars burn out. Most creatures choose to serve.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Bind a creature of CR 3 or lower for one task of up to 24 hours. The creature obeys the letter of the command but may exploit loopholes. It cannot harm you directly. |
| Standard (9-14) | Bind a creature of CR 5 or lower for one month of service. It must obey any command that isn't directly self-destructive. It can be given a standing order it will follow until completed. It may attempt a Reason check once per week to break free. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Bind a creature of CR 7 or lower for a year and a day of service. It serves loyally unless you give it a command that violates its fundamental nature. It will interpret your commands in good faith. It can be assigned to guard a location, serve as an advisor, or fight at your side. Breaking the binding requires a ritual that takes at least a full day. |

*This is how summoners become legendary. Planar Binding is not a combat spell. It's a campaign spell. You bind something from beyond the material plane and it works for you for a month, a year, forever. The demon lord's lieutenant? Now she's your bodyguard. The angel who refused to help? Now they don't have a choice. The line between summoner and slave-master is thin, and Planar Binding walks it with both feet. Use it carefully. Bound things remember. And bindings, eventually, break.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Shadow Chains

Shadow magic is the art of the space between. Not darkness, darkness is just the absence of light. Shadow is the presence of something else, something that lives in the gaps between what's real and what's almost real. Shadow mages don't hide. They step sideways, into a world that's one degree removed from this one, and when they step back, they're somewhere else entirely.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Cloak of Shadow Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*From dimming the light to walking between worlds to becoming the darkness itself.*

#### Cloak of Shadow (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 10 minutes
**Target:** Self

**Description:** Shadows gather around you like a living cloak. They don't make you invisible, but they make you *less.* Less noticeable. Less memorable. Less there. Light seems to slide off you. Eyes seem to skip past you. You're not hiding. You're just not worth noticing.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Stealth checks have +1. The shadows are thin, bright light diminishes the effect. Duration 1 minute. |
| Standard (9-14) | Stealth checks have Boon. You can attempt to hide even when only lightly obscured. Creatures that saw you hide must make a Reason check to remember exactly where you were. Duration 10 minutes. |
| Strong (15-18+) | As Standard, plus you can meld into an existing shadow large enough to contain you. While melded, you can't move but are invisible and silent. You can remain melded for up to 1 minute or until you take an action. |

*The first shadow spell. It won't make you a ghost. It'll make you a maybe. "Was someone standing there a moment ago?" "Probably just the light." By the time they finish the thought, you're somewhere else, and the only evidence you were ever there is a shadow that's slightly darker than it should be.*

#### Shadow Step (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 Maneuver
**Range:** 60 feet
**Duration:** Instantaneous
**Target:** Self

**Description:** You step into one shadow and out of another. The space between is cold, silent, and very, very brief. One moment you're here. The next, you're there. Anyone watching sees the shadows flicker and you're just... somewhere else. It's not teleportation. It's taking a shortcut through somewhere that doesn't quite exist.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | Teleport 20 feet to a shadow you can see. The transition is disorienting, your next action has -1. |
| Standard (9-14) | Teleport 60 feet to any shadow you can see or have seen within the last minute. You arrive silently. You have Boon on your next attack before the end of your turn, striking from an unexpected angle. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Teleport 100 feet to any shadow you've ever seen in the current location. You may bring one willing creature within 5 feet with you. Both of you arrive with Boon on your next attack. You can use this to escape grapples, restraints, and non-magical bonds automatically. |

*The spell that makes shadow mages impossible to pin down. Enemy has you cornered? There's a shadow under their boot. Trapped in a cell? There's a shadow in the corner. Falling off a cliff? There's a shadow on the cliff face if you're quick enough. Shadow Step doesn't just move you. It redefines what "here" and "there" mean, and it makes the enemy's careful positioning completely irrelevant.*

#### Shadow Form (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Wind
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** Self

**Description:** You stop being a creature that casts shadows and become a shadow that happens to look like a creature. Your body loses its edges. Light passes through you. Weapons pass through you. You slide along walls and under doors. You are a two-dimensional piece of darkness with a will and a purpose, and solid matter is just a suggestion you've decided to ignore.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | You become a shadow. You can move through spaces as narrow as 1 inch. You have resistance to non-magical damage. You cannot attack or cast spells while in shadow form. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | Shadow form. You can move through any gap, along walls, and across ceilings. Immune to non-magical damage. You can make one attack per round while in shadow form, your strikes emerge from the target's own shadow. Spells of Novice tier can still be cast. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Full shadow form. Immune to all damage except radiant and force. You can cast any spell while in shadow form. You can attempt to possess a creature's shadow, forcing them to mimic your movements (Hard Reason check to resist). You can travel through the Shadowfell, effectively teleporting up to 1 mile by spending 1 round in the in-between. Duration 1 minute. |

*This is what the darkness has been saving for you. Shadow Form doesn't make you harder to hit. It makes hitting you conceptually difficult. Swords pass through darkness. Arrows find no purchase in shadow. Spells lose their target because their target has stopped being a thing and started being an absence. For one minute, you're not a combatant on the battlefield. You're a patch of darkness that the enemy's nightmares forgot to warn them about.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Arcane Weapon Chains

An arcane weapon is a spell you can hold. It's a blade of force, a hammer of fire, a spear of lightning given physical form. Weapon mages don't stand in the back and throw spells. They wade into melee with a sword made of pure magic and remind everyone that the line between "wizard" and "warrior" is a suggestion, not a rule.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Arcane Blade Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*Conjure a weapon of magic. Enhance it with element. Forge it into a blade that cuts through reality itself.*

#### Arcane Blade (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** 1 minute
**Target:** Self

**Description:** A weapon of shimmering force materializes in your hand. It can be any melee weapon shape you choose, a sword, an axe, a spear. It weighs nothing. It never dulls. It doesn't need to be drawn from a sheath, it just is, and when you swing it, it cuts with magical precision that steel can't match.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The blade deals 2 force damage. It flickers but holds. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | The blade deals 4 force damage. You use your spellcasting attribute for attack rolls instead of Brawn or Agility. It counts as magical for overcoming resistance. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | The blade deals 6 force damage and gains one property of your choice: reach (10-foot range), thrown (20/40 feet, returns after attack), or finesse (can use Agility for damage). Duration 1 minute. |

*Your first weapon that isn't a weapon. Arcane Blade is for the mage who's tired of being squishy. For the Arcanist who wants to look the enemy Blade in the eye and say "you and me, right now, and I brought my own sword." It's not as powerful as a Fireball. But Fireball doesn't let you parry. Fireball doesn't let you feel the impact run up your arm when you connect. Fireball is a spell. This is a statement.*

#### Elemental Weapon (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Touch
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** One weapon

**Description:** You infuse a weapon (your Arcane Blade, your ally's sword, a random chair leg) with elemental fury. Flames wreathe the blade. Lightning crackles along the edge. Frost crusts the hilt. The weapon doesn't just hurt. It burns, it shocks, it freezes. Every swing is a spell and a strike at the same time.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The weapon deals +2 damage of your chosen element (fire, ice, or lightning) on each hit. It sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | The weapon deals +4 elemental damage per hit. On a Strong attack result, the element flares: fire ignites the target (1 ongoing), ice slows (speed halved 1 round), lightning stuns (no reaction). Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | The weapon deals +6 elemental damage per hit. The elemental effect triggers on any hit, not just Strong results. The weapon's damage type counts as both its base type and the element (whichever is more advantageous). Once during the duration, you can unleash the element in a 15-foot cone dealing 6 damage of that element to all creatures in the area. |

*Give this to your Blade. Watch their eyes light up. Watch the enemy's eyes go wide. Elemental Weapon takes a mundane problem (someone needs stabbing) and applies a magical solution (the stabbing now comes with fire). It turns every swing into a light show. It turns your frontline fighter into a walking spell delivery system. And if you cast it on your own Arcane Blade, you've got a weapon that's equal parts sword and spell, and you're about to ruin someone's entire day.*

#### Blade of Disaster (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Wind
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** Self
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** Self

**Description:** You call into existence a blade that isn't made of matter, isn't made of force, isn't made of anything that exists in the normal sense. It's a planar rift shaped like a sword. It cuts through armor, flesh, bone, reality itself, with equal indifference. The blade hums with wrongness. Things it cuts don't just die. They come apart at the seams, and the seams don't always go back together.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The blade deals 9 force damage. It ignores 2 points of Armor. It can damage ethereal creatures and objects as if they were solid. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | The blade deals 15 force damage. Ignores all Armor. A creature killed by the blade cannot be resurrected by Novice or Adept spells, the death is too fundamental. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | The blade deals 21 force damage. Ignores Armor and damage resistance of any kind. Hits automatically sever one non-magical object the target is holding or wearing (your choice). On a Strong attack result, the target must make a Fortitude check or lose a limb (DA's choice, context-dependent). The blade leaves wounds that resist magical healing, any healing on the target is halved until the end of its next long rest. |

*This is the weapon at the end of everything. Blade of Disaster isn't a spell you cast lightly. It's a declaration. You're not fighting anymore. You're ending things. Every swing is a small apocalypse. Every hit is a reminder that the universe is mostly empty space held together by rules, and you've decided the rules don't apply to this particular sword. When you dismiss the blade, it leaves a faint scar in the air where it was, a line of nothing that takes a few seconds to heal. Even reality needs a moment to recover from what you just did.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Gravity Chains

Gravity is the oldest magic in the universe, and the most patient. It doesn't burn. It doesn't freeze. It just waits, and pulls, and never gets tired. Gravity mages don't throw things at the enemy. They make the enemy heavy. They make the ceiling the floor. They make the air itself press down like a fist the size of the sky. Gravity magic is subtle until it isn't, and when it stops being subtle, everyone within a hundred feet finds out what they really weigh.

*See @sec-chapter-magic-system for how spellcasting works.*

### Burden Chain
**Disciplines:** Energy
*From extra weight to crushing pressure to inverting the fundamental forces that hold the world together.*

#### Burden (Novice)
**Disciplines:** 1 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** One creature or object

**Description:** You point, and the target suddenly weighs twice as much as it did a moment ago. Armor becomes a prison. Weapons become anchors. The charging enemy becomes a staggering mess trying to figure out why their own body has betrayed them. Gravity doesn't need to hurt. It just needs to be heavier than you are.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | The target's weight increases by half. Speed reduced by 5 feet. Attacks have -1. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | Weight doubled. Speed halved. Attacks have Bane. Flying creatures are grounded. The target cannot jump or climb. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | Weight tripled. Speed reduced to 5 feet. Attacks have Bane. The target is knocked prone and cannot stand until the spell ends. Flying creatures take 4 bludgeoning damage as they crash to the ground. |

*The first gravity spell. It's not flashy. It's not destructive. It's just physics, weaponized. Cast Burden on the enemy knight in full plate and watch them sink to their knees. Cast it on the fleeing messenger and watch their sprint become a stagger. Cast it on the flying creature and watch the sky reject them. Gravity is patient. Be patient with it.*

#### Crushing Force (Adept)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 60 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** 10-foot radius

**Description:** You designate an area and gravity there becomes *angry.* Everything in the zone is pressed down as if a giant's hand is pushing from above. Bones creak. Armor deforms. Creatures are flattened to the ground, struggling to breathe, struggling to move, struggling to exist in a space where the universe has decided they weigh a thousand pounds.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 5-foot radius. Creatures take 6 force damage and are slowed (speed halved, no reactions). Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | 10-foot radius. Creatures take 9 force damage per round. They are restrained (cannot move, attacks have Bane). Flying creatures are crushed to the ground and take double damage for the first round. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 15-foot radius. 12 force damage per round. Creatures are restrained and must make a Fortitude check each round or be incapacitated, unable to take actions at all. Objects in the area take double damage. Fragile structures (wooden floors, furniture) collapse. |

*Gravity stops being patient. Crushing Force is an area of "you don't get to move anymore." Drop it on the enemy formation. Drop it in a doorway. Drop it on the bridge the enemy is trying to cross and watch the bridge decide it would rather be somewhere else. Everything in that circle is now subject to a gravitational field that wants them flat, and gravity always gets what it wants.*

#### Reverse Gravity (Master)
**Disciplines:** 2 Energy, 1 Earth
**Casting Time:** 1 action
**Range:** 100 feet
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 minute
**Target:** 20-foot radius cylinder, 40 feet high

**Description:** You point up, and the universe shrugs and says "fine, that way is down now." Everything in the area falls upward. Creatures tumble into the sky, arms flailing, dignity abandoned. Objects become projectiles. The ground becomes the ceiling. And when you stop concentrating, everything falls back down. The fall up is disorienting. The fall down is terminal.

| Outcome | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Weak (1-8) | 15-foot radius, 30 feet high. Creatures fall upward 20 feet, taking 9 bludgeoning if they strike a ceiling. When the spell ends, they fall back down for standard falling damage. Duration 3 rounds. |
| Standard (9-14) | 20-foot radius, 40 feet high. Creatures fall upward to the top of the cylinder (40 feet) and hover there, unable to move, taking 15 force damage per round from the gravitational stress. When the spell ends, they fall for full falling damage. Ranged attacks from within the zone have Bane, projectiles curve unpredictably. Duration 1 minute. |
| Strong (15-18+) | 30-foot radius, 60 feet high. Creatures are hurled to the top in one round and pinned there, restrained and incapacitated. 21 force damage per round. You may release individual creatures from the effect, letting them fall early. Creatures that strike a solid surface on the way up take double damage. When concentration ends, you choose whether creatures fall or are lowered gently. |

*This is the spell that makes gravity mages unforgettable. Reverse Gravity doesn't just damage, it rewrites the battlefield's relationship with down. The enemy formation becomes a cloud of flailing bodies forty feet in the air. The archers on the battlement fall up into the sky. The carefully organized battlefield becomes chaos in three dimensions. When you cast Reverse Gravity, you're not fighting the enemy anymore. You're fighting the concept of "ground," and you're winning.*

```{=typst}
#horizontalrule
```
